newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-FINLAND BEAT U.S. 2-0 TO FINISH FIFTH.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-FINLAND BEAT U.S. 2-0 TO FINISH FIFTH.

text.p: Finland beat the United States 2-0 on Friday to finish fifth and deny the Americans the chance to play for bronze in the ice hockey world championship pool A tournament.

The victory marked an emotional farewell for Finnish head coach Curt Lindstrom, whose four-year term at the helm of the national team came to an end -- a couple of days too early for the home side, which had counted itself among the title favourites.
The U.S. had needed a win or a draw to finish fourth and grab a berth in the bronze final, but host goalkeeper Ari Sulander denied them, stopping all 22 shots. The U.S. ended sixth.
Russia and titleholders the Czech Republic will play for the bronze on Saturday. Earlier on Friday, Canada defeated Russia 2-1 to earn a place in the best-of-three final starting on Sunday.
Antti Aalto scored the opening goal in the second period, breaking through in the middle and beating NHL Chicago Blackhawks netminder Christopher Terreri with a snappy low shot.
Teppo Numminen added a second goal right at the start of the third period with a thundering slapshot from a superb flip pass by Ville Peltonen of the San Jose Sharks.
